title: High Dimensional First Order Mini-Batch Algorithms on Quadratic Problems
extraction: Exact original SVG polygon/polyline vertices. Affine normalization x=(X-144)/892.8 and y=(633.60006-Y)/554.40006; no fitted curve, smoothing, simulation, or invented data.

semantics.bands: The source caption calls these the 90th percentile confidence interval. Exact quantile endpoints and number of replicates are not specified here.
semantics.dimension: d/n is fixed. The numeric value and the covariance used for this figure were not identified in the paper or located original code; neither is inferred from related experiments.
semantics.prediction: One original Volterra prediction is drawn for all four n values within each method. The predictions differ between the two methods.
semantics.caution: The original bands need not be nested, symmetric, centered on the prediction, or contain it at every iteration. They are confidence bands, not individual trajectories.
semantics.neighboring_spectrum: The neighboring Marchenko–Pastur spectrum is a separate finite-dimensional illustration with its own specified covariance and aspect ratio. Sharing the sample-size presentation clock does not identify it with the experiment that generated these paper bands.

presentation.palette: Original geometry recolored warm sage for bands and rust for the fixed prediction; stroke styling is adapted for the small header.
presentation.animation: Smoothstep opacity-only crossfades and holds between the four original confidence polygons in n=64,256,1024,4096 order. Each band opacity is proportional only to its shared-clock weight; inactive bands have exactly zero opacity. The original prediction stays visible throughout the fade/reset. No intermediate sample sizes or coordinate interpolation between bands.
presentation.static: Only the original n=4096 confidence polygon plus the unchanged prediction; all other bands have zero opacity.
presentation.scale: Original plot aspect ratio and logarithmic vertical-coordinate mapping are retained.
presentation.progress_marker: A shared marker tracks weighted checkpoint index. It represents presentation progress, not an intermediate computed sample size.
presentation.reduced_motion: Initially show the largest-size still, with an explicit Play motion opt-in. Pausing after opt-in freezes the dynamic phase.

verification.shared_progress_marker: finite, normalized, monotonic across checkpoint growth; fades out before loop reset
